sanskrit: yā te tanūr apacakrāma mṛtyor devānāṃ sakhyam abhi jīvalokam | apsucarā gahvareṣṭhā mahitvā tasyām eṣaḥ suhuto astv odanaḥ so asmākam astu parame vyoman ||
english: That body of yours which departed from Death toward the fellowship of the gods, toward the world of the living — she who roams the waters, she who dwells in the depths, in her greatness: may this oblation-rice be well-offered to her; may it be ours in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: aheḍamānābhy ehi no gṛhaṃ saṃkāśaṃ bhadre sumanā aghorāḥ | prati tvā varṣavṛddham etu ||
english: Without wrath, come back to our house, auspicious one, with gracious mind, not terrible — may the rain-grown [offering] go forth to meet you.

sanskrit: eṣā naḥ svadhā navagaj janitry amṛteṣv amṛtāhutābhūt | tān no gopāya sadam apramādam āsmākam aitor anu rakṣa jāgṛhi ||
english: This our svadhā — the nine-fold mother — has become an immortal oblation among the immortals. Guard those [forebears] for us always, without negligence; they have come to us — watch over them, be wakeful.

sanskrit: ye no nidhim abhidāsanty etaṃ pravāhaṃ proḍhaṃ yamarājye | rājā teṣāṃ varuṇa indriyāṇy abhi tiṣṭḥatu harasā daivyena | etaṃ sadhasthāḥ pari vo dadāmy anukhyātā yajñapatir yad āyat ||
english: Those who assail this deposit of ours — the current carried off into the realm of Yama — may king Varuṇa stand over their vital faculties with divine wrath. Those who sit together in this assembly: I give you this [deposit] in full, for the lord of sacrifice has come, having beheld it.

sanskrit: ya ākhidanti vikhidanti dattaṃ vi gṛhṇate dakṣiṇā nīyamānāḥ | tān indro devo maghavāñ chacīpatir agnimedī pradahann etu śakraḥ | bṛhaspatir varuṇaḥ soma indro mamaiva dattaṃ kevalaṃ kṛṇvantu ||
english: Those who scratch away and tear apart what has been given, who seize the sacrificial fee while it is being conveyed — let Indra the god, the bountiful, lord of Śacī, mighty Śakra, come burning them with the fire-kindler's flame. May Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Soma, and Indra make what I have given solely and wholly mine.

sanskrit: śīrṣaktiṃ śīrṣāmayaṃ karṇaśūlaṃ tṛtīyakam | sarvaṃ śīrṣaṇyaṃ te rogaṃ bahir nirmantrayāmahe ||
english: Headache, head-disease, earache, tertian fever — all the ailment in your head we charm out and away.

sanskrit: karṇābhyāṃ te kaṅkūṣebhyaḥ śuktivalgaṃ vilohitam | (…) ||
english: From your ears, from your ear-passages — the oyster-shell discharge, the bloody [flux] — [we charm out and away].

sanskrit: yaḥ kṛṇoti pramotam andhaṃ kṛṇoti pūruṣam | (…) ||
english: That [disease] which renders a man stupefied, which renders a man blind — [we charm it out and away].

sanskrit: yasya hetoḥ pracyavate yakṣmo nāsata āsyataḥ | (…) ||
english: On whose account wasting-disease (yakṣma) falls away from the nose and from the mouth — [we charm it out and away].

sanskrit: śīrṣarogam aṅgarogaṃ viśvāṅgīnaṃ visalpakam | sarvaṃ śīrṣaṇyaṃ te rogaṃ bahir nirmantrayamahe ||
english: Head-disease, limb-disease, the disease that pervades all limbs, visalpaka — all the ailment in your head we charm out and away.

sanskrit: yasya bhīmaḥ pratīkāśa udvepayanti pūruṣam | takmānaṃ śītaṃ rūraṃ ca taṃ te nir mantrayāmahe ||
english: Whose terrible appearance makes a man tremble — fever-ague (takman), the chill, and the burning: that we charm away from you.

sanskrit: ya ūrū anusarpaty atho ye 'nu gavīnike | balāsam antar aṅgebhyo bahir nirmantrayāmahe ||
english: That which creeps along the thighs and also along the groins — balāsa (phlegmatic disease) from within the limbs we charm out and away.

sanskrit: yadi kāmād apakāmād dhṛdayāj jāyate pari | hṛdo balāsam aṅgebhyo bahir nirmantrayāmahe ||
english: Whether from desire or from aversion it is born and spreads from the heart — balāsa from the heart, from the limbs, we charm out and away.

sanskrit: harimāṇaṃ te aṅgebhyo yakṣmodhām antarātmanaḥ | yakṣmaṃ te sarvam aṅgebhyo bahir nirmantrayāmahe ||
english: Jaundice (harimāṇa) from your limbs, the nest of wasting-disease from within your inner self — all yakṣma from your limbs we charm out and away.

sanskrit: āso balāso bhavatu mūtraṃ bhavatv āmayat | yakṣmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ nir avocam ahaṃ tvat ||
english: Let the balāsa become raw discharge; let the ailment become urine. The poison of all wasting-diseases I have now spoken out away from you.

sanskrit: bahir bilaṃ nir dravatu kahāvāhaṃ tavodarāt | yakṣmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ nir avocam ahaṃ tvat ||
english: Let the hollow drain outward — the kahā-bearer from your belly. The poison of all wasting-diseases I have now spoken out away from you.

sanskrit: udarāt te pari klomno nābhyā hṛdayād adhi | yakṣmodhām antarātmano bahir nir mantrayāmahe ||
english: From your belly, round about from your kloman (right lung), above from your navel, from your heart — the nest of wasting-disease from within your inner self we charm out and away.

sanskrit: yāḥ sīmānaṃ virujanti mūrdhānaṃ pratyarṣaṇīḥ | ahiṃsantīr anāmayā nir dravanti bahir bilam ||
english: Those [diseases] that break through the crown of the head, that flow back against the summit — may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening.

sanskrit: yā hṛdayam upasarpanty anutanvanti kīkasāḥ | (…) ||
english: Those that creep toward the heart and stretch along the vertebrae — [may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening].

sanskrit: yāḥ pārśve uparṣanty anunikṣanti pṛṣṭīḥ | (…) ||
english: Those that flow up along the flanks and pierce along the ribs — [may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening].

sanskrit: yās tiraścīr uparṣanty arṣaṇīr vakṣaṇābhyaḥ | (…) ||
english: Those that flow up crosswise, the flowing ones from the flanks — [may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening].

sanskrit: yā gudā anusarpanty āntrāṇi yopayanti ca | (…) ||
english: Those that creep along the rectum and also constrict the intestines — [may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening].

sanskrit: yā majjño anusarpanti parūṃṣi virujanti ca | ahiṃsantīr anāmayā nir dravanti bahir bilam ||
english: Those that creep along the marrow and also break apart the joints — may they, no longer harming, free of affliction, run outward through the opening.

sanskrit: ye aṅgāni madayanti yakṣmāso ropaṇāsaḥ | yakṣmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ nir avocam ahaṃ tvat ||
english: Those wasting-diseases that intoxicate the limbs, the festering ones — the poison of all wasting-diseases I have now spoken out away from you.

sanskrit: visalpakasya vidradhasya vātīkārasya vālajeḥ | yakṣmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ nir avocam ahaṃ tvat ||
english: Of visalpaka, of vidradha (abscess), of vātīkāra (wind-disease), of vālaja — the poison of all wasting-diseases I have now spoken out away from you.

sanskrit: pādābhyāṃ te kulphābhyāṃ jaṅgābhyāṃ jānubhyām ūrubhyāṃ śroṇibhyāṃ pari bhaṃsasaḥ | anūkyād arṣaṇīr uṣṇihābhyo grīvābhyaḥ skandhebhyaś śīrṣṇo rogam anīnaśam ||
english: From your feet, from your ankles, from your shins, from your knees, from your thighs, from your hips, round about from your buttocks — from the spine, the flowing discharges, from the nape, from the neck, from the shoulders, from the head: I have caused the disease to perish.

sanskrit: saṃ te śīrṣṇaḥ kapālāni hṛdayasya ca yo viduḥ | udyan sūrya ādityo 'ṅgarogam anīnaśat ||
english: The skull-plates of your head and of the heart — those who know them: the rising sun, Āditya, as he ascends, has caused the limb-disease to perish.
